standard.title: High-frequency words and homophones
standard.description: recognise and know how to write most high-frequency words including some homophones
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use contextual and syntactic knowledge to spell some homophones (referenced in Y2). They have not yet focused on reliable recognition and writing of most high-frequency words as a distinct target, or on using context systematically to identify correct homophone spelling.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and write most high-frequency words including some homophones.

nodes.label: High-frequency word recognition and writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and write most high-frequency words automatically.
nodes.minimum_width: Read and write at least 20 high-frequency words correctly and automatically (without sounding out).
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and write most high-frequency words automatically in both reading and writing contexts, including in extended writing tasks.
wider: Identify which high-frequency words are still causing errors in personal writing and develop a targeted strategy to learn those specific words
Examine how high-frequency words are often irregular and cannot be decoded phonically — discussing what strategies work for learning these words

response_modes.reason: High-frequency word recognition is built through repeated encounters — it is essentially a memorisation task. Practice and exposure are the mechanisms, not conceptual extension.

success_criteria: Student reads high-frequency words without decoding (automatic recognition)
Student writes high-frequency words correctly in the context of their own writing

nodes.label: Homophones and context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use context and syntactic knowledge to identify and spell the correct form of common homophones.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly select and spell the right homophone (e.g. 'break' or 'brake', 'their' or 'there') in at least three sentence contexts and explain how the context was used to decide.
nodes.typical_width: Use context and syntactic knowledge to spell homophones correctly — identifying common homophone pairs and applying context clues to select the right form in reading and writing.
wider: Find homophone errors in a passage and explain how to use context clues to correct each one
Explore less common homophones encountered in reading and build a personal reference list with example sentences for each

response_modes.reason: Homophone selection errors persist because students learn word forms in isolation rather than in context. Multiple different sentence contexts for each homophone pair help students develop reliable context-based discrimination.

success_criteria: Student selects the correct homophone form in a sentence context
Student can explain how the sentence context signals which form is correct
